title: Bandwidth Governor and Soft Burst Fabric — PRD (WIP)
content:
Summary:

This PRD proposes a new Dedicated-capacity feature set: the Bandwidth Governor and Soft Burst Fabric. The goal is to reduce noisy-tenant impact on latency-sensitive tenants while enabling predictable, cost-efficient microbursting and controlled opportunistic bursting. This blends credit-based burst tokens, per-tenant bandwidth envelopes, and a soft preemption/stepping policy that prefers graceful degradation over hard throttles.

Why this is needed (problem statement):
- Many tenants require low tail latency even during platform-wide demand spikes; totally hard isolation (hard cgroups, immediate preemption) solves correctness but wastes capacity and damages customer experience.
- Existing reserved capacity + naive burst credits lead to either over-provisioning or large noisy-neighbor incidents.
- Customers want a notion of "bandwidth" (tokens/sec or tensor-flops/sec) tied to latency envelopes rather than raw GPU allocation.
- Ops needs predictable failure modes and a clear escalation/playbook when bursts collide.

Goals (measurable):
- Keep P95 latency for latency-tier customers within 1.3x baseline for 99% of burst events (target: 99.5% of bursts).
- Allow tenants to consume up to 3x baseline sustained throughput for short windows (up to 120s) using burst credits, without causing >30% latency regression to high-priority tenants.
- Provide operators with signal and automated mitigation so human intervention is required in <5% of collision events.
- Expose per-tenant bandwidth profile and historical burst cost to customers in Console.

Non-goals:
- Full rewrite of scheduler or tenant billing model. This is an evolution implemented as a runtime policy layer + control-plane features.

User stories:
- "As a product engineer, I want my latency tier to be prioritized so occasional noisy neighbors don't blow up my P99 so I can meet SLAs."
- "As a platform engineer, I want predictable rules that let some tenants burst opportunistically while preventing long tail impact on other tenants."
- "As an SRE on call, I want clear runbook steps and automated mitigations to reduce toil during high contention nights."

High-level approach (three pillars):
1) Bandwidth Envelopes: represent tenant capacity as a bandwidth envelope (units: compute-tokens/sec). Each tenant has a baseline sustained envelope derived from their reserve and historical throughput; envelope determines their guaranteed pacing.
2) Soft Burst Fabric: tenants accumulate burst credits when they are below baseline; credits are spent to temporarily expand their envelope. Credits decay and replenish with time.
3) Isolation & Grace Policies: when contention occurs, apply a layered policy chain: adaptive pacing -> priority-aware micro-preemption -> soft-eviction margins -> fallback routing (spill to hosted-compatible model variant). The idea is preference for smoothing/stepping instead of immediate eviction.

Design details:
- Compute tokens: unitized metric mapping request size, seq len, and model cost to a "token cost" (similar to existing per-token cost but normalized to runtime CPU/GPU usage). Runtime needs a low-latency estimator per-request.
- Envelope calculation: baseline_bandwidth = committed_pool_compute_tokens_per_sec * tenant_committed_fraction. For shared pools with no commit, baseline derived from moving-average of recent 15m consumption with floor set to a small reserve.
- Burst credits: tenants accrue at accrual_rate = baseline_bandwidth * accrual_factor (default 0.2) up to cap = baseline_bandwidth * burst_window_seconds (default 120s). Credits are consumed at request-time proportional to request cost.
- Tier-aware behavior: tenants assigned tier (latency, standard, bulk). Bandwidth governor treats tiers differently: latency-tier has higher preservation of baseline and lower accrual-to-cap ratio for others.

Burst modes (distinct):
- Microburst: <5s high-intensity spikes. Handled by token borrowing with negligible preemption; best-effort smoothing via batching and quick KV-cache reuse.
- Short burst: 5–120s using burst credits. Preferred path uses credits before affecting other tenants.
- Opportunistic burst: allowed when node has idle margin (observed utilization < X% for Ys). These bursts are marked revocable and can be reclaimed quickly.

Isolation controls & collision handling:
- Latency envelope enforcement: runtime monitors per-tenant moving-window latency. If a tenant's increase would push latency-tier tenants above target, the governor will throttle opportunistic bandwidth to preserve targets.
- Noise threshold detection: if a tenant's request mix (large batch, long sequence) suddenly spikes, label as noisy and move into a soft-quarantine for T_quarantine seconds, during which its accrual and opportunities to burst are reduced. This is reversible if pattern normalizes.
- Grace preemption: instead of hard preempting GPU kernels, we first reduce concurrency slots, increase batching windows for the offender, and inject backpressure at the front-end. If still insufficient, migrate low-priority work off the node to ephemeral host or queued backlog.
- Fallback routing: a configurable route can be used to send overflow requests to hosted-compatible model variants (slightly smaller model or slower latency SLO) with clear cost/billing separation.

Control plane features:
- Per-tenant bandwidth profile UI: shows baseline, current envelope, credit balance, recent bursts and cost.
- Policy editor: allow customers to choose conservative/elastic modes, set burst caps, and opt-in to opportunistic bursts.
- Alerts & metrics: automatic alerts when cross-tenant contention is detected, and playback traces for the last 30s of enforced decisions.

Operational playbook (short):
- Detect: SRE paging rule triggers on pool-wide P95 breach + high variance across tenants.
- Mitigate auto: governor reduces opportunistic bursts by 30% immediately, enforces soft-quarantine on tenants above noise threshold and routes new work to spare pools or hosted fallback if configured.
- Manual: SRE investigates tenant-level telemetry in Console. If an offending customer is legitimate, follow customer engagement runbook; otherwise escalate to support for rate-limiting.

Telemetry & SLOs to instrument:
- Per-tenant: current_bandwidth_usage, credit_balance, average_request_cost, P50/P95/P99 latency, noisy_event_count.
- Per-pool: utilization, spare_margin_seconds, revocable_work_ratio, number_of_quarantined_tenants.

Fail-safes and billing implications:
- If governor cannot restore SLOs automatically, fallback to hard-eviction after a configurable grace window (default 30s). Hard-eviction emits audit event and sets tenant into recovery cooldown.
- Billing: bursts should be metered separately and surfaced in invoices. We will add burst_cost_by_window to billing pipeline and expose an estimated burst-cost in Console during consumption.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Where to place the compute-token mapping: runtime at edge vs central estimator? Edge is lower latency but harder to update; central allows consistent mapping but adds RTT.
- How aggressive should accrual be for multi-tenant pools? Higher accrual improves customer experience but increases collision risk.
- How to bill for opportunistic bursts in shared pools fairly (pro rata vs usage-based)?

Prototype plan & milestones (quarterly):
- Week 0–4: implement lightweight compute-token estimator in runtime and a credit accounting shim (no enforcement) — collect signals.
- Week 5–10: implement enforcement paths in a canary pool (soft throttles, quota checks, quarantines) + Console telemetry.
- Week 11–16: add fallback routing and billing metering for burst windows, run chaos tests simulating noisy neighbors.
- Week 17–24: expand to 50% of dedicated pools, run customer pilot (2 latency-tier customers), iterate on accrual policies.

Risk matrix and mitigations:
- Mis-estimation of compute tokens -> mis-weights bursts: mitigation: conservative initial mapping, heavy telemetry, and rapid rollback toggle.
- Billing surprises for customers -> mitigation: show estimated burst costs before charges, soft opt-in for first N bursts.
- Complexity overload for ops -> mitigation: a simple default policy that works for 80% cases and advanced policies behind feature flags.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Create Linear tickets for runtime estimator, credit ledger, quarantine feature, UI surfaces (assigned to Luca).
- Schedule platform SRE tabletop to walk through playbook and failure cases (Radhika to coordinate).
- Draft customer-facing docs explaining burst accounting and expected behavior.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a hybrid token that mixes bandwidth + memory footprint for large KV reuse to avoid memory-saturating bursts.
- Could map burst credits to a marketplace where tenants can temporarily buy extra credits at premium pricing.
- Think about exposure of historical burst events in the SDK so devs can programmatically detect high-cost windows.

Appendix: quick glossary
- baseline_bandwidth: sustained compute-tokens/sec guaranteed under reserve.
- compute-token: normalized unit representing request cost on runtime.
- accrual_rate/cap: rate at which burst credits accumulate and max balance.
- soft-quarantine: temporary policy state reducing burst privileges for a tenant showing noisy behavior.

End of draft.

References and links: see linked_artifacts above; also relevant existing PRDs in dedicated folder (search: "burst" and "isolation") for context.
